topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure and sets out the key learning objectives regarding the environmental causes and mechanisms of cancer.

topics.label: The Multifactorial Origins and Epidemiology of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from an interplay between intrinsic cellular processes, inherited genetics, and external exposures as demonstrated by population-level epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms through which infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular link between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how various environmental chemicals, dietary toxins, and radiation undergo metabolic processing and directly alter DNA structure to cause mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and the Initiation-Promotion Paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how non-mutagenic agents foster cancer development by creating inflammatory microenvironments and stimulating cell proliferation to promote initiated cells.

topics.label: Host Developmental Susceptibility and Summary of Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how tissue context and stages of life modulate cancer vulnerability, before reviewing the primary mechanisms through which carcinogens act.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the scientific approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and identify exposures through genomic sequencing, epidemiological biobanks, animal testing, and bacterial assays.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Evaluation and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on the challenges of determining carcinogenic potency and the everyday calculation of exposure risks versus benefits.
